known.why: candor-java's `unverified --class` has not landed the §6.2 ⟨0.24⟩ repair that rust, ts and swift all carry. Query.java's filter tests `f.unknownReasons()` — the DIRECT `unknownWhy` — so it (1) never resolves the class set transitively, and (2) never CONTRIBUTES `unresolved` to a function whose direct Unknown carries no reason. The counterexample therefore reads inverted: `--class unresolved` selects NOTHING at all (0 of 3), and `--class dispatch` selects only the source, not the two callers that inherit from it. The GATE half of this row is clean on java — `deny Unknown[unresolved]` exits 2 (the answerability refusal), fail-closed — which is exactly §6.2's 'the gate had never been party to the defect: the divergence was entirely consumer-side, in the one query that reads a REPORT rather than the scan's in-memory graph, and which carried an open-coded second copy of the classification'.
repro: HAND-WRITTEN report r.json (no scan, no compiler):
{ "candor": {"version":"handwritten","spec":"0.23"}, "package":"app",
"analyzed": {"count":3,"digest":"0"}, "functions": [
{"fn":"app.a","inferred":["Unknown"],"calls":["app.src_reasonless"]},
{"fn":"app.src_reasonless","inferred":["Unknown"],"direct":["Unknown"],"unknownWhy":[]},
{"fn":"app.src_reasoned","inferred":["Unknown"],"direct":["Unknown"],"unknownWhy":["dispatch:app.Base.run"]} ] }
plus r.callgraph.json = {"app.a":["app.src_reasonless"],"app.src_reasonless":[],"app.src_reasoned":[]}
and a policy file containing `pure app`.
java -jar candor-java-all.jar unverified --report r.json --policy pol --json --class unresolved
java  -> []                        candor-rust / candor-ts / candor-swift -> [app.a, app.src_reasonless]
... --class dispatch
java  -> [app.src_reasoned]        the other three -> [app.b, app.c, app.src_reasoned]
The fix is the one §6.2 names: hoist the transitive class fixpoint and the match rule into the
code the gate already uses, rather than patching the consumer's second copy.
